[P2] Run the new mixed-layout coverage in the default test build

This setup is compiled out when `TRON_K_VNNI` (the key-layout build option) is off. The default continuous-integration workflow, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`, builds through `nix/tron-build.nix` and `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix`. Its CMake arguments omit both `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` and `TRON_K_VNNI`. Both default to off.

The affected test binaries are registered and selected by the host suite. Their new feature-specific checks therefore do not exercise mixed layouts in that workflow. The legacy CMake workflow enables both options, but it now runs only through manual dispatch or workflow calls.

The disabled options predate this diff. The new concern is that the coverage added here does not run in the default test build, contrary to the repository's test policy. Enable these checks in an existing required test suite. Validate this by showing that a deliberate break in row-major-tail dispatch fails that suite.

Agreed on the facts. The setup at t_llama_unit.cpp:1943 and the VNNI (Vector Neural Network Instructions, the pair-interleaved K layout) branches of `check_blocks` compile only with `TRON_K_VNNI` (the K-layout build option). The default CI (continuous integration) lane is the gcp-nix.yml workflow, which runs on every pull request. It builds the test runtime through nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix. That configure line sets neither `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` (the option that compiles the AMX kernels; AMX = Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions) nor `TRON_K_VNNI`. Both default to OFF (CMakeLists.txt:48-49). The only lane with both options on is the legacy workflow cmake-single-platform.yml (lines 333-334). It runs on manual dispatch, or from publish-deb.yml (the Debian package workflow) for tag and feature-branch publishes. No pull request runs it.

The gap predates this PR. PR #3879 added `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` to the legacy lane (f4889f8072) and PR #4424 added `TRON_K_VNNI` (929fa94e42). By then the CI cutover (the move of the default CI to the nix lane, 2f1ee29982, 2026-09-11) had already made the legacy lane manual. The PR #4424 body records that the default CI builds its benchmark binary with neither option, and the test runtime comes from the same build. This PR adds 627 test lines in three files with the same gap: 81 lines compile only under `#ifdef TRON_K_VNNI`, and the rest pick their VNNI branch through `k_vnni::layout_on`, which is false without the option.

What a fix needs. The mixed-layout coverage needs no AMX hardware. The dense AMX path is gated on `amx_q_packed` and on every block of the page holding the VNNI layout (`k_vnni_blocks` equal to `k_vnni::ALL_BLOCKS_0XF`). The VNNI reader `k_vnni::qk_group` is AVX-512 BF16 code (512-bit vector instructions, no AMX tiles). Every CI runner with the labels `[self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512]` executes that code. So adding `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON -DTRON_K_VNNI=ON` to nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix would make the Test host job (a required check on every pull request) run these tests. The cost is a policy choice. `TRON_K_VNNI` is a PUBLIC compile definition (a CMake term: every target that links tron inherits it) [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:209-213]. So every test in the default lane would then run the VNNI layout. The per-commit benchmark runtime, built from the same compilation (nix/tron-build.nix), would run it too. The shipped package uses the row-major layout. The row-major branches of the tests that have a VNNI branch would no longer run in the required suite. One configuration cannot run both branches. Running both needs a second test runtime. That touches the handoff scripts (bin/ci/tron-build/prepare_handoff.py, which passes the built runtime to the test jobs) and the required check names.

Not changed in this PR:

- The nix lane belongs to the CI owner.
- The layout choice for the whole suite belongs to the reviewers of #4424.
- AGENTS.md (the repository's instructions for coding agents) says an agent may not grant the test-policy exception.

Options for the author and the CI owner to pick:

- (a) Add the two flags to nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix in #4424. That is one line plus a README.ci.md paragraph. The precedent is PR #4505, which added `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` to the deb preset (the CMake preset that builds the Debian package).
- (b) Add a second configuration to the nix test build. Both layouts then run on every pull request.
- (c) Run cmake-single-platform.yml by hand on the final head and link the run from the PR, as evidence until (a) or (b) is merged.

I did not run the deliberate-break check. It needs a CI run of a lane this PR does not trigger. The unit tests at 9e813a8ce5 ran on delphi-3bda (our Intel test machine) in both builds (`TRON_K_VNNI` ON and OFF). The PR body has the result.

[P3] Pass the storage reference as one concept

This adds a separate layout-state index to an existing five-parameter interface. `k_storage_ref` (the physical storage offset paired with its layout-state index) already names the relationship introduced by this change.

Readers now have to reconstruct that relationship at each copy and conversion call. EAGLE storage, used for speculative decoding, makes the distinction relevant: its physical offset and state index can differ.

Pass `k_storage_ref` here and to `k_block_to_vnni_at`, the conversion helper. Keep the source page and copy-range arguments explicit. This is a readability improvement; I did not find an incorrect mapping in the current callers.

Agreed, and changed in d8f6c479bc.

- `copy_storage_slot` and `k_block_to_vnni_at` take one `k_storage_ref` (the storage offset paired with its layout-state index). `copy_storage_slot` is back to five parameters. The source page and the copy range stay explicit.
- `k_block_to_vnni` and `convert_pending_k_blocks` pass the ref through instead of splitting it.
- `copy_from` builds the ref for each physical slot at the call: `{kv_storage_offset(slot), slot}` and `{book.eagle_storage_offset(), layout_t::n_slots}`. It does not go through `k_storage_of`. `k_storage_of` follows the current storage view. A page copy moves every physical slot.
- The bodies unpack the ref once. The bit logic and the copy loops are unchanged.
- The comment on `k_storage_ref` now says how `copy_from` builds the pair.

Agreed, and changed in a9923ddd97. The clause described the row-major branch of `get_k_row`. The staging callback no longer takes that branch. For a row-major block the callback returns the row pointer from `page::k_row_if_row_major`. It calls `get_k_row` only for a converted block. Item 4 now says that. It also names Note [Row-major blocks under hardware attention]. That note says why the row-major case is the usual one under hardware attention.

One change to the suggested text. "v_head_fn copies the value row" holds only when `TRON_CHUNK_SIZE` (the SIMD vector width in 32-bit lanes) is 16, the AVX-512 build. A build with any other value returns `page::v_ptr` in place (the `#else` branch in full.hpp). The new text states both forms. The remark inside the callback in full.hpp ("The V callback below always copies.") is corrected the same way.
